<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914115_theRebbe_704" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914115_theRebbe_704__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header and date for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B"S.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Haazinu,</t>
    <t s="2">Shabbos Shuvah 5741*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the verse "Shuvah Yisrael" and the Alter Rebbe's explanation, raising questions about how teshuvah applies to one on the level of Yisrael.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Return, O Yisrael, unto Hashem your G-d, for you have stumbled in your iniquity."</t>
    <t s="1">And the Alter Rebbe explained,</t>
    <t s="2">that what is written "Return... unto Hashem your G-d"</t>
    <t s="3">(even though ostensibly it should have said "to Hashem your G-d")</t>
    <t s="4">means,</t>
    <t s="5">that the measure of teshuvah is until Hashem becomes your G-d.</t>
    <t s="6">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="7">that one who is relevant for</t>
    <t s="8">(and is required of him)</t>
    <t s="9">such an exalted teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="10">is surely a person of an exalted level even before performing this teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="11">as is also understood from what is written "Shuvah Yisrael,"</t>
    <t s="12">for the name Yisrael is because "you have striven with G-d and with men and have prevailed,"</t>
    <t s="13">meaning he is a prince</t>
    <t s="14">and rules over the concealment of the name Elokim and over the powers that spread forth from it</t>
    <t s="15">("men"),</t>
    <t s="16">and how can the matter of iniquity, which would require teshuvah, apply to him?</t>
    <t s="17">And although it is known that teshuvah is not only for transgressions</t>
    <t s="18">but rather to return one's soul to its source and root</t>
    <t s="19">["and the spirit returns to G-d who gave it"],</t>
    <t s="20">for this teshuvah applies even to completely righteous individuals,</t>
    <t s="21">nevertheless, the verse explicitly states "Shuvah Yisrael... for you have stumbled in your iniquity,"</t>
    <t s="22">and how can the matter of iniquities apply to one who is on this level?</t>
    <t s="23">Also, it needs to be understood what the verse continues,</t>
    <t s="24">"Take words with you and return to Hashem,"</t>
    <t s="25">for after already saying "Shuvah Yisrael," what is added by</t>
    <t s="26">("Take words with you")</t>
    <t s="27">"and return to Hashem"?</t>
    <t s="28">Also, it needs to be understood what it says afterwards,</t>
    <t s="29">"Say to Him, 'Forgive all iniquity,'"</t>
    <t s="30">for even the saying and request "forgive iniquity" is connected to the matter of teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="31">and from this it implies that after the teshuvah of "Shuvah Yisrael" and of "return to Hashem,"</t>
    <t s="32">there needs to be yet another teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="33">Also, it must be said that in the first teshuvah and in the third teshuvah the matter of iniquity is mentioned</t>
    <t s="34">("for you have stumbled in your iniquity,"</t>
    <t s="35">"forgive iniquity"),</t>
    <t s="36">but not in the second teshuvah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that there are three levels of teshuvah corresponding to the three verses, based on Likkutei Torah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And the point of the explanation regarding this is according to what is explained in Likkutei Torah,</t>
    <t s="2">that in teshuvah there are three levels.</t>
    <t s="3">Teshuvah of "turn away from evil,"</t>
    <t s="4">teshuvah of "and do good,"</t>
    <t s="5">and teshuvah of "seek peace," which refers to the Torah, for all who engage in Torah make peace in the heavenly retinue and in the earthly retinue,</t>
    <t s="6">and the entire Torah was given to make peace in the world.</t>
    <t s="7">And the three teshuvahs in these verses</t>
    <t s="8">["Shuvah Yisrael...,"</t>
    <t s="9">"and return to Hashem,"</t>
    <t s="10">"say to Him, 'Forgive all iniquity'"]</t>
    <t s="11">are the three teshuvahs of "turn away from evil," "and do good," and "seek peace."</t>
    <t s="12">And this is also why these verses are the beginning of the haftarah of Shabbos Teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="13">for on Shabbos Teshuvah all three levels must be present.</t>
    <t s="14">And as my father-in-law, the Rebbe, related,</t>
    <t s="15">that by the Tzemach Tzedek on Shabbos Teshuvah there were three candles of teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="16">and the Tzemach Tzedek said, "There are three teshuvahs,"</t>
    <t s="17">and my father-in-law, the Rebbe, explained that they are the three teshuvahs explained in Likkutei Torah.</t>
    <t s="18">And this is why in the first teshuvah it is written "Return... for you have stumbled in your iniquity,"</t>
    <t s="19">but not in the second teshuvah</t>
    <t s="20">("and return to Hashem")</t>
    <t s="21">is the matter of iniquity not mentioned,</t>
    <t s="22">for the first teshuvah is the teshuvah of "turn away from evil"</t>
    <t s="23">("you have stumbled in your iniquity"),</t>
    <t s="24">but the second is the teshuvah of "and do good."</t>
    <t s="25">And this is also why in the first teshuvah the name Elokim is also mentioned</t>
    <t s="26">("unto Hashem your G-d")</t>
    <t s="27">and in the second teshuvah only the name Hashem is mentioned</t>
    <t s="28">("and return to Hashem")</t>
    <t s="29">and in the third teshuvah it is written "say to Him,"</t>
    <t s="30">for the teshuvah of "turn away from evil" is that Hashem should be our G-d,</t>
    <t s="31">and the teshuvah of "and do good" is to connect and cleave to the name Hashem as He is above the name Elokim,</t>
    <t s="32">and the teshuvah of "seek peace" is to cleave and be included in the Atzmus of Ein Sof, which is above the name Hashem.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
